summary.headline: IEX Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose about 12% to Rs 134.8 crore on Rs 202.8 crore revenue, with electricity volume up 16% to 37.5 billion units.
summary.overview:
IEX reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 202.8 crore and PAT of Rs 134.8 crore, up about 12% YoY, on electricity volume of 37.5 billion units (+16%). Real-Time Market growth was the main driver, with RTM up about 25% in Q1 and its share of mix reaching about 34% last year. Management used the analyst meet to push a set of new products (Green RTM, peak contracts, 11-month TAM, carbon trading, coal exchange) while pushing back on CERC's proposed market coupling and the Day-Ahead Market pilot, which it has challenged at APTEL and the Supreme Court. The call was mostly a policy and product narrative; no formal FY27 guidance was given.</overview>

segments.name: Electricity (DAM / RTM / TAM)
segments.commentary: RTM is now roughly the size of DAM; DAM share of mix fell from 95% in FY16 to about 39%, RTM rose to about 34% in FY26, and RTM is up about 25% in Q1 FY27. Term-Ahead Market and Green Market are about 7-8% of the mix.

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange, associate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 42 crore; Q1 FY27 volume 27.5 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 16 crore. DRHP filed for IPO of a 22.3% stake to bring IEX's 47.3% holding down to 25% under PNGRB rules, after a one-year extension.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC / environmental)
segments.commentary: Sole I-REC issuer in India; management cited about 200% growth in I-REC volumes last year. Q1 REC volumes were down sharply YoY, which management attributed to the first quarter and possible RPO buy-out confusion.

segments.name: Indian Coal Exchange (new)
segments.commentary: Incorporated as a separate company in June 2026; coal rules notified 4 June 2026 require e-auction and marketplace trades to move to exchanges within six months of launch. Market size cited at about 120 million tonnes today, with a target of at least 100 million tonnes in year one.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 volume or revenue guidance given; management expects RTM volumes to grow about 25-30% a year.
Management expects carbon credit trading to begin in FY27, with BEE targeting 1 October 2026.

Management expects the Green RTM, peak-power contracts (DAM and RTM) and 11-month TAM products to be approved by CERC; timing was not committed, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending for over two years.
Management sees the exchange-routed share of electricity rising to about 25% over five to six years, against about 14-15% short-term market today.
Management said it would consider a buyback in future, citing SEBI's revised market-buyback rules.
Management said the coal exchange's fee should exceed those of MSTC and M-Junction, since exchanges perform price discovery, clearing and settlement.
capex_capacity: Management cited about 80 GW of thermal capacity in the pipeline, 41 GW under construction with PPAs signed, 20 GW awarded, and 16 GW in planning; most is expected in FY31-FY33.
Management said it has built a hot standby for RTM and a DC-to-DR switch; both were positioned as ready for the proposed 5-minute bidding window.

BESS merchant capacity cited: ACME about 3,200 MWh, Juniper about 500 MWh, Adani about 3,400 MWh, with more than Rs 9,000 crore of BESS VGF support. Management said the arbitrage window may last 3-5 years.
The SECI 500 MW CfD pilot for peak power was cited as launched; it is a peak-power product, not solar.
demand_pricing: Management expects demand growth of about 5-5.5% a year, versus 11% in Q1 FY27 on heat and delayed monsoon. Peak demand touched about 271 GW in May and July.
Management said exchanges as a group grew 18% in FY26 against 1% demand growth.

On market coupling, CERC proposed Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, with DAM first. Management said it has challenged the July 2025 order at APTEL (order dated 13 February 2026) and is now before the Supreme Court; a second hearing was held on 27 July 2026.
Management said that even after coupling, DAM share could fall 20-40%, but said business impact would not be significant. The market-share loss figure is management's own estimate.
Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side and the top-buyer concentration is 50-60%, with 800-900 participants daily.

Management cited an RTM realisation issue in a Q&A: an analyst's per-unit realisation calculation (about 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa a year earlier) was not reconciled; management pointed to incentives in REC and TAM.
